subject.title: Feature Request: Enforce skill execution sandbox when enabled: false

question: Should `skills.entries.<key>.enabled:false` become a hard read/exec access boundary for that skill, or should hard isolation use a separate explicit policy while `enabled:false` remains a visibility and eligibility toggle?
rationale: The source-level gap is clear, but either outcome changes a security boundary and compatibility expectations across skills, filesystem tools, exec, sandboxing, UI/status, and docs.

options.title: Add explicit strict isolation policy
options.body: Keep `enabled:false` compatible as a visibility/eligibility toggle, add a separate operator-controlled hard isolation policy, and make the UI/docs distinguish the two states.

options.title: Make disabled mean hard deny
options.body: Treat `enabled:false` as a central deny boundary for disabled skill roots across read, write/edit/apply_patch where relevant, exec, sandbox materialization, UI/status, and docs.

options.title: Document current semantics only
options.body: Leave the runtime unchanged and make docs/UI say disabled skills are hidden from discovery, while sandboxing, OS users, and tool policy own hard isolation.

recommendation.title: Add explicit strict isolation policy
recommendation.body: Keep `enabled:false` compatible as a visibility/eligibility toggle, add a separate operator-controlled hard isolation policy, and make the UI/docs distinguish the two states.

likelyOwner.reason: This is primarily a security/product boundary choice, and the strongest current history signal ties this person to the central code and skill security hardening.
